adapters.exportDuty: STATELESS: the counters are a per-colo burst bound that expires within its own period (10 or 60 seconds) and record nothing. Export: nothing. Cannot move: nothing — a switch is a config change, and the budgets are the `ratelimits` blocks of each wrangler.jsonc.

c8Seam.why: tooling/capability-register.json records Cloudflare's C-8 seam as the client's ConfigTransport (the config the apps fetch). The Rate Limiting binding is one of several Cloudflare surfaces now behind its own port; the vendor's C-8 row is re-seated when its last surface, D1, is ported.

adapters.exportDuty: A test double: a fixed-window counter that lives for one test. Nothing to export.

pending.case: the whole suite against the real binding: every Worker suite runs on Node under plain vitest (services/*/vitest.config.ts), not on workerd — no Miniflare, no @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers — so the binding never meets the suite in CI; the structural proof is tsc over ports/adapters/cloudflare.ts

_why: Every `*_LIMITER` binding (services/platform, services/edge-shield) is declared as RateLimiterBinding, which is now the RateLimiter port re-exported by services/_shared/src/rate-limit.ts; the platform's limiters are reached only through that module's withinRateLimit / strictRateLimit / edge-ceiling helpers, and the edge shield's through its own fail-open `ask`. The failure policy stays with those callers; the port carries none.

L2 claimed, L2 target: selected by environment, no caller imports an adapter, one live adapter. A Workers Rate Limiting binding satisfies the port STRUCTURALLY; cloudflareRateLimiter is the identity, kept as the compile-time proof.

The conformance suite runs against the memory fake; against the binding it is PENDING, because no Worker suite runs on workerd (and the binding is per-colo and eventually consistent, so even there an over-budget answer is not deterministic).
